passage.text: Nam's grandmother grew up in a small village by a river.
passage.reading: ˈnɑːmz ˈɡrænmʌðər ˈɡruː ˈʌp ɪn ə ˈsmɔːl ˈvɪlɪdʒ baɪ ə ˈrɪvər.

passage.text: Her family had a small house and a big rice field.
passage.reading: hɜːr ˈfæməli ˈhæd ə ˈsmɔːl ˈhaʊs ənd ə ˈbɪɡ ˈraɪs ˌfiːld.

passage.text: There was no electricity in the village, so at night they used oil lamps.
passage.reading: ðɛr wʌz ˈnoʊ ɪˌlɛkˈtrɪsəti ɪn ðə ˈvɪlɪdʒ, soʊ ət ˈnaɪt ðeɪ ˈjuːzd ˈɔɪl ˌlæmps.

passage.text: Every morning, she used to walk to school with her brothers and sisters.
passage.reading: ˈɛvri ˈmɔːrnɪŋ, ʃiː ˈjuːst tə ˈwɔːk tə ˈskuːl wɪð hɜːr ˈbrʌðərz ənd ˈsɪstərz.

passage.text: After school, she used to help her parents in the rice field.
passage.reading: ˈæftər ˈskuːl, ʃiː ˈjuːst tə ˈhɛlp hɜːr ˈpɛrənts ɪn ðə ˈraɪs ˌfiːld.

passage.text: The family had two buffaloes, and she loved riding them.
passage.reading: ðə ˈfæməli ˈhæd ˈtuː ˈbʌfəloʊz, ənd ʃiː ˈlʌvd ˈraɪdɪŋ ðɛm.

passage.text: On hot afternoons, all the children used to swim in the river.
passage.reading: ɑːn ˈhɑːt ˌæftərˈnuːnz, ˈɔːl ðə ˈtʃɪldrən ˈjuːst tə ˈswɪm ɪn ðə ˈrɪvər.

passage.text: "We didn't have TV or phones, but we were happy," she says.
passage.reading: wiː ˈdɪdənt ˈhæv ˌtiːˈviː ɔːr ˈfoʊnz, bʌt wiː wɜːr ˈhæpi, ʃiː ˈsɛz.

passage.text: She still lives in the village, and she still keeps her old oil lamp.
passage.reading: ʃiː ˈstɪl ˈlɪvz ɪn ðə ˈvɪlɪdʒ, ənd ʃiː ˈstɪl ˈkiːps hɜːr ˈoʊld ˈɔɪl ˌlæmp.

passage.text: When Nam visits, her grandmother talks about the past.
passage.reading: wɛn ˈnɑːm ˈvɪzɪts, hɜːr ˈɡrænmʌðər ˈtɔːks əˈbaʊt ðə ˈpæst.
